header.prompt: Multi-part: how the pieces are made
Test log: every pull after test 1
Which printer: X1 Carbon or H2D
What it did, if none of the choices fit

blocks.prompt: V1 hook type: standard or multi-part
V1 part file (piece A)
Screenshot of V1 with the feature tree
Feature tree: any red or yellow?
V1 measurements against the rules, with a fix for any that miss

criteria.text: The V1 part files are handed in, named, and rebuild

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Every part file the hook needs is handed in (one for a standard hook or a piece printed twice, one per piece otherwise), named V1_ or V1A_, V1B_, V1C_ with the student's last name, opens, is a whole hook rather than a start, and shows no red or yellow marks in the tree.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: A whole hook that opens, but the tree carries red or yellow marks, or a name does not follow the pattern.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: The file is still a start (a sketch or a partial body), or a multi-part hook is missing a piece.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: No part file handed in.

criteria.text: The screenshot shows the whole part and a readable tree

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: The whole SolidWorks window: the solid part and the full FeatureManager tree, readable.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: The part shows, but the tree is cropped, collapsed, or too small to read.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: No screenshot uploaded.

criteria.text: Every dimension is measured on the model, and every one outside the rule has a fix

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Every row carries a number measured on the student's own model, and every row outside the rule says what changes and by how much.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: One row has no measurement, or one row outside the rule has no fix.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: The numbers repeat the rule rather than the model, or two or more rows are missing.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: No measurements entered.

blocks.prompt: Nozzle set in the slicer
Plate type set in the slicer
Filament profile set in the slicer
Full-size weight from the slicer, grams
Half-scale weight from the slicer, grams
Is the half-scale weight one eighth of full size? If not, why
Slicer preview screenshot
At the thinnest spot: solid walls or infill, and why it matters in a pull
Printer name or number from the print board

criteria.text: The half-scale test copy is set up right and printing

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Nozzle, plate and Generic ABS picked to match the printer, lying flat so the pull runs along the layers (seen in the preview), 50 percent, one plate with every piece of this one hook on it, and the printer it is running on named.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: The copy is printing, but it is standing up, the wrong size, missing a piece, or sharing a plate with someone else.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: No test copy sliced or started.

criteria.text: The layer preview screenshot shows the estimated weight

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: A screenshot of the sliced layer preview with the filament weight readable.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: A screenshot of the part, but not sliced, or the weight is not in the picture.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: No screenshot uploaded.

criteria.text: Both weights are read off the slicer and the full size is judged against 50.0 g

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Full-size and half-scale weights from the slicer, the full size judged against 50.0 g, and a reason the half scale is or is not one eighth.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: One or both weights, with no comparison to the cap or no reason.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: No weights entered.

criteria.text: Says whether the thinnest part is solid walls or walls with infill, and why that matters under a pull

levels.label: Complete
levels.short: Found it, and why it matters
levels.descriptor: Names where the part is thinnest, what the preview shows there, and why that matters for a part pulled until it breaks.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Says walls or infill without the place or the reason.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Nothing written.

blocks.prompt: Date of test 1
Prediction: where will it break, and why there
Breaking load from the score sheet, lb
Kept the broken pieces
Photo 1 of the break
What the hook did when it failed
Where on the part it broke
Was the prediction right?
One thing the next version changes because of it

criteria.text: The copy is pulled at the rig, the load is recorded, and the pieces are kept

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Pulled at the rig, the breaking load written down from the score sheet, and the pieces kept.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Pulled at the rig, but the load is not recorded or the pieces were not kept.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: No pull recorded.

criteria.text: The fracture photos are close, in focus, and show the broken face

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: At least one photo that is close, in focus, and shows the broken face.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Photos of the break that are blurry, far away, or do not show the broken face.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: No photo uploaded.

criteria.text: Says where it broke on the part and how it failed

levels.label: Complete
levels.short: Place on the part, and mode
levels.descriptor: Names the exact place on the part, and picks how it failed: snapped, pulled open, layers split, the joint let go, or something else described.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Names the place but not the mode, or the mode but not the place.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Says it broke with no place and no mode.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Nothing written.

criteria.text: The call is written before the pull and checked honestly after

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: A call made before the pull, right, half right or wrong picked after, and one thing the next version changes because of it. A wrong call earns the same as a right one.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: The call is checked, but nothing says what changes next, or the call is too vague to check.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: No call, or no check.
